This document contains the full paper in English followed by the full
paper in Chinese (p. One Byte, One Token: Byteifying a 27B
Hybrid-Attention LLM with Self-Generated Data). Both versions describe
the same experiments and report the same numbers.

## 1 Introduction

A subword tokenizer is a design decision frozen before training. For
Chinese, Qwen3.8’s byte-level BPE averages 3.84 bytes per token on
Chinese Wikipedia, 64% of tokens are single characters
(tokenizer-eval/), and a word is often split into several fragments; for
every language, spelling, character positions and the individual digits
of numbers are invisible to the model, so character-level operations
must rely on ”thinking” to break a word apart before acting on it
(Section 5.4). Once the vocabulary is fixed, all subsequent training and
serving are bound to it.

The most direct alternative is a byte model: 1 byte = 1 token, a
vocabulary of 256 plus special symbols. Training a byte model from
scratch is too expensive; the two existing practical routes each carry a
cost\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94keep a patching structure (local
encoder + patches, as in BLT and Bolmo), in which case the backbone
still sees patched vectors; or do cross-tokenizer distillation through a
byte-level interface (still judged an open problem at 1B–8B). This paper
takes a third route: convert an already-trained 27B subword model, as
is, into a pure byte-level model without patching, replacing only the
vocabulary and embeddings and leaving the backbone untouched.

Our approach is: shrink the vocabulary to 384 (the BPE vocabulary
already contains 256 byte symbols), then continue training with a
two-stage curriculum\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94first learn the
”character $`\leftrightarrow`$ bytes” encoding from the character
dictionary, the word dictionary and dialogue, then read human-written
encyclopedia text (Section 3). All dialogue/behavioral supervision is
generated by the original Qwen3.8 itself (on-policy self-distillation,
with per-turn independent re-answering and supervising only the current
turn); knowledge reading uses human-written text (54% of supervised
bytes). The whole run uses 4.77 GB of supervised bytes and takes 178.6 h
on 8$`\times`$H200.

This paper sets out to answer only four questions, which are also its
four contributions:

1.  1.  How much is retained (Sections 5.1, 5.2): a two-column comparison on
        the same GPU, the same serving stack and the same decoding protocol.
        In non-thinking mode, 4 of 7 items show no detectable difference
        within the paired bootstrap interval, while C-Eval and non-thinking
        IFEval drop 4–6 points; in thinking mode, GSM8K $`-`$4.0 and C-Eval
    $`-`$4.5.
2.  2.  What bytes bring (Section 5.4): without thinking, character-level
        operations lead across the board (CUTE +8.8, EXECUTE-zho +12.2, our
        Chinese character suite +9.7), with larger margins in Chinese than
        in English; but lookup knowledge about Chinese characters such as
        pronunciation and stroke count drops, and thinking does not recover
        it.
3.  3.  What it costs (Section 5.6): per-step speed is identical, but each
        step yields 3–5$`\times`$ less output; on the same GPU, Chinese
        characters per second falls to 1/4, and prefill at 64K bytes is
        6.5$`\times`$ slower; a draft head is the way to recover speed, but
        it does not fit on a single 48G GPU.
4.  4.  Failure modes specific to byte models, and their fixes (Section 6):
        greedy runaway, byte-wise sampling breaking UTF-8, penalty terms
        being ineffective on a small vocabulary, and thinking that cannot
        find its way out; together with the corresponding decoding guard and
        post-training methods.

We do not claim that the byte model is stronger. The honest conclusion
is: at 27B scale and a continued-training budget of about 1e21 FLOPs,
byteification without patching can match most of the original model’s
ability, gaining character-level operations at the cost of throughput
and part of the character-level knowledge. The evaluation scripts, our
Chinese character suite, and the scoring / bootstrap code for every
evaluation in this paper are available at
https://huggingface.co/datasets/leiwhere/ld3-byte-eval; the weights and
the training corpus are not released at this time.

## 2 Related Work

Byte- and character-level models trained from scratch. ByT5
\[[25](#bib.bib25)\] feeds T5 raw UTF-8 bytes and is an early
representative of ”flat bytes”; CANINE \[[3](#bib.bib3)\] and Charformer
\[[22](#bib.bib22)\] shorten the character sequence with downsampling or
differentiable soft subwords; MEGABYTE \[[28](#bib.bib28)\], SpaceByte
\[[21](#bib.bib21)\], BLT \[[14](#bib.bib14)\] and H-Net
\[[10](#bib.bib10)\] build patching into the
architecture\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94fixed-length,
whitespace-based, entropy-based or end-to-end learned
boundaries\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94and run the backbone over
the patches. MambaByte \[[23](#bib.bib23)\] and EvaByte
\[[31](#bib.bib31)\] keep flat bytes but respectively switch to an SSM
backbone or train a 6.5B model from scratch. All of these works train
from scratch; our starting point is different: whether a subword model
that has already been trained on tens of trillions of tokens can be
converted directly into a byte model without retraining the backbone and
without adding a patching structure.

Converting subword models into byte models. BLT reports an experiment
that initializes the global Transformer from Llama 3.1 8B (220B tokens),
keeping patching and a newly trained local encoder/decoder
\[[14](#bib.bib14)\]. Bolmo \[[13](#bib.bib13)\] does this
systematically: Olmo 3 7B is converted into a byte-level ”latent
tokenizer language model”, with bytes pooled into patches and an mLSTM
local encoder/decoder, about 49B tokens over two stages in total (39.3B
in the second stage); patching is likewise kept, and the backbone runs
over patches. [Bao et al. \[1\]](#bib.bib1) uses progressive
distillation to align a token teacher’s representations to an
H-Net-style hierarchical byte student ($`\leq`$ 4B). [Singh et al.
\[20\]](#bib.bib20) uses bytes only as the interface for cross-tokenizer
distillation, with the student still a subword model, and reports that
consistent gains at 1B–8B ”remain hard to obtain”. The inference-time
method of \[[9](#bib.bib9)\] involves no training and turns any BPE
model into a byte-level sampler, while the model internally still
computes over subwords. Compared with these, this paper (i) does no
patching at all, with the backbone taking one step per byte; (ii)
introduces no external teacher, with supervision coming from the
original model’s own outputs and human-written text; (iii) works at 27B
scale with a focus on Chinese, and reports the efficiency cost on the
same GPU. The cost of not patching is that the sequence length is not
compressed, which Section 5.6 reports as is.

Vocabulary transfer. ZeTT \[[12](#bib.bib12)\], FOCUS \[[5](#bib.bib5)\]
and TokAlign \[[11](#bib.bib11)\] study how to initialize new embeddings
and recover in a few steps when switching to a different subword
tokenizer. This paper is the extreme case: the new vocabulary has only
the 256 byte symbols left, and these 256 rows are already in the
original embedding table (GPT-2-style byte-level BPE
\[[18](#bib.bib18)\]), so no initialization trick is needed and all of
the difficulty shifts to continued training.

Self-generated data and on-policy training. Self-Instruct
\[[24](#bib.bib24)\], STaR \[[30](#bib.bib30)\] and RFT
\[[29](#bib.bib29)\] train a model on its own (filtered) outputs; SDFT
\[[27](#bib.bib27)\] has the seed model rewrite task answers to mitigate
forgetting; [Chen et al. \[2\]](#bib.bib2) attributes the reduced
forgetting of RL to on-policy data. Our corpus recipe (Section 3.2) and
post-training (Section 3.4) rest on the same
observation\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94dialogue supervision must
be the target model’s own current
output\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94and apply it to the setting of
vocabulary replacement, a drastic distribution shift; DPO
\[[19](#bib.bib19)\] is used as the means of controlling repetition,
with length normalization.

Base model and benchmarks. Qwen3.8-27B \[[17](#bib.bib17)\] is a dense
model mixing Gated DeltaNet \[[26](#bib.bib26)\] and full attention at a
3:1 ratio (see \[[16](#bib.bib16), [15](#bib.bib15)\] for descriptions
of the same architecture family), and natively carries one MTP layer
\[[8](#bib.bib8), [4](#bib.bib4)\]. Character-level tasks use CUTE
\[[6](#bib.bib6)\] and its multilingual extension EXECUTE
\[[7](#bib.bib7)\].

## 3 Method

### 3.1 Vocabulary Shrinking

The tokenizer of Qwen3.8-27B is a GPT-2-style byte-level BPE: the
vocabulary already contains 256 single-byte symbols, and every
multi-byte token is formed by merging them. Converting to a pure byte
model therefore requires no new embeddings at all; we only delete every
merge entry and keep the 256 byte rows plus the special symbols that the
chat template depends on. The shrunk vocabulary has 384 entries: bytes
0–255 ordered by byte value, followed by 35 named special symbols such
as \<\|endoftext\|\>=256, \<\|im_start\|\>=257 and \<think\>=280, with
the remaining 93 positions as placeholders (full table in Appendix B).
The tokenizer contains no merge rules whatsoever: one UTF-8 byte is one
token.

The backbone is left untouched: 64 layers = 48 GatedDeltaNet layers + 16
full-attention layers (one every 4 layers), hidden size 5120, model_type
still qwen3_5, so off-the-shelf inference frameworks load it directly.
Parameters change only at the two ends: the embedding and the lm_head
each shrink from 248,320 $`\times`$ 5,120 $`\approx`$ 1.27B to 384
$`\times`$ 5,120 $`\approx`$ 2M, and the language-model part goes from
26.9B to 24.4B; the 0.46B vision tower is frozen as is. The shrinking
script selects rows by token name rather than by id offset; the output
is checked item by item against the special-id table and the md5 of the
chat template (two easily missed errors: the vision token ids in the
config, and the reordering of special symbols by newer versions of
transformers).

The cost is longer sequences: the original tokenizer averages 3.84
bytes/token on Chinese and 4.35 on English, so byte-level sequences are
about 4$`\times`$ as long, and a 16K-byte window corresponds roughly to
4k BPE tokens. In Chinese text, only 15.9% (digits, punctuation,
newlines) already falls on single-byte tokens, and 99.4% of Chinese
characters never pass through the byte path in the original model, so
the zero-adaptation model can read but reads poorly: the untrained
shrunk checkpoint has four-domain bpb of zh 3.02 / en 4.43 / code 2.54.
These numbers serve only to check that the shrinking was done correctly
(they are of the same order as the zero-adaptation numbers of the first
27B pilot) and are not taken as a measure of starting ability.

### 3.2 Corpus: Self-Generated Dialogue Supervision, Human-Written Text for Knowledge Reading

Across its two-stage curriculum, LD3-base read 7.08 GB in total, of
which 4.77 GB were supervised bytes. Supervised bytes by source: wiki
text 2.56 GB (54%), word dictionary 1.61 GB (34%), character dictionary
0.30 GB (6%), general dialogue 0.16 GB, coding sessions 0.14 GB. To be
clear from the outset: the wiki, which accounts for 54% of supervised
bytes, is human-written Wikipedia text, read in pretraining fashion,
concatenated end to end and cut into windows; it is not model-generated.
What is self-generated is the other four categories of dialogue /
behavioral supervision. The human text is responsible for knowledge
reading; the self-generated dialogue is responsible for ”the model
speaking in its own words in bytes”.

All dialogue supervision is generated by the original Qwen3.8-27B itself
(on-policy), on the basis of two sets of controlled comparisons. Among
the six ”less thinking” training comparisons on the Ornith pilot lines,
only training the model on its own current outputs came at zero cost
(3.2 passes over its own correct samples, accuracy unchanged at 49%),
whereas all four recipes that used data written by others lost 5–14
points, regardless of content quality; ”current” is strict enough that
outputs from one training stage earlier no longer count. A three-arm
comparison in cross-vocabulary distillation points to the same thing:
supervising prompt prefixes written by others made code bpb 26% worse
and en 16% worse, and the damage disappeared once supervision was
restricted to the current turn’s generation. Hence, in this paper, CE is
computed only on assistant turns (including thinking); multi-turn
sessions use per-turn independent re-answering, with the prefix kept
verbatim and supervising only the current turn.

The four self-generated corpora are: (1) the character dictionary,
12,126 Chinese characters (8,105 standard characters + 4,021 traditional
characters whose written form differs from the simplified one), with
readings, senses and simplified–traditional relations taken from Unihan
/ CC-CEDICT / OpenCC, three dialogue turns per character (entry
$`\rightarrow`$ translate the whole entry into the other language
$`\rightarrow`$ follow-up question); it is the most direct explicit
supervision of ”one character $`\leftrightarrow`$ three bytes”, and so
comes first. (2) The word dictionary, 141,361 entry seeds $`\times`$ 4
turns. The writing rule for both dictionaries is ”facts come from the
dictionary, the wording is written by the teacher”: prompts are natural
dialogue, format requirements are placed only in the unsupervised user
turn, and the persona is spread over 33 variants so that the writing
style is not pulled toward a single persona. (3) General dialogue,
60,549 sessions after deduplicating six public session pools, 1.13
million assistant turns in total, 91% of which are agent turns with tool
calls. (4) Human coding sessions, two public datasets (6,772 + 1,064
sessions) re-answered twice per turn, 88,743 turns in total. All
generation was done with thinking on and the official sampling
parameters (temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20).

The amount generated far exceeds the amount used in training: more than
300,000 turns of general dialogue were generated locally, yet only 0.16
GB of supervised bytes entered the curriculum, because prefixes are long
and only the last turn is supervised. Local generation totaled about
94.9 h $`\approx`$ 760 H200 GPU-hours; for the part that went through
hosted APIs (2,048 essays, about 11,800 logic problems, coding sessions)
the compute is not visible and only call volumes are reported. Essays
and logic problems did not enter the two-stage curriculum of LD3-base:
the logic problems (reasoning-gym, 99 categories, 10,560 problems, 9,618
answered correctly) are used in Section 3.4, and the essays (two
batches, about 2,560 in total) were only generated and never entered any
training pack.

### 3.3 Two-Stage Curriculum: Learn the Encoding First, Then Read

All training is full-parameter with ZeRO-3, and checkpoints store
weights only (47 GB). Both stages use a constant learning rate; between
stages only the weights are carried over (optimizer reset, 5 warmup
steps), and no bpb regression was observed in practice. Decisions were
made by looking jointly at four-domain byte bpb, a 30-problem greedy
probe and a held-out dialogue set; no decision was made on any one of
them alone.

M1 (encoding stage) (64K-byte window, 2,077 steps, lr 3e-6, 47.5 h):
character dictionary : word dictionary : general dialogue mixed 1:1:1 by
supervised bytes, with the character dictionary used in full for one
pass, the word dictionary sampled for character coverage, and general
dialogue restricted to sessions that fit entirely within 64K. Actually
read: 1.143 GB; supervised: 0.616 GB (the ”0.28 GB each, 0.85 GB total”
in the training records is the sampling target; this paper uses the pack
statistics). The bpb trajectory shows that ”Chinese is the new skill”:
en reaches 0.58 within 100 steps and stays there, while zh goes from
3.02 through 1.12 at step 400 to 0.900 at the end. But at the end of M1
the model can read without being able to use what it reads: the probe
scores 29/30, yet ”English $`\rightarrow`$ Chinese” terminology scores
0/12 while the English paths score
11–12/12\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94the knowledge is there; what
is broken is the link between Chinese word forms and concepts.

M2 (reading stage) (16K-byte window, 6,761 steps, lr 5e-6, three
continuation segments totaling 131 h): wiki text : general corpus : word
dictionary = 1:1:1 mixed by item count, which in supervised bytes is
wiki 54% / word dictionary 34% / dialogue 6% (Section 3.2), because
dialogue prefixes carry no loss. Actually read: 5.932 GB; supervised:
4.156 GB. After M2, ”English $`\rightarrow`$ Chinese” terminology went
from 0/12 to 12/12 (already reached at 3,000 steps), the probe to 30/30,
and GSM8K in dialogue form to 294 of 300 problems; MMBench-CN rose from
65.2% to 72.2%, so text-only training did not harm the frozen vision
tower.

Both stages mix, never sequence: on the pilot lines, the recipe ”train
on the narrow corpus first, then patch with normal data afterwards”
pushed the behavior back, but the lost abilities did not return; so M1
mixes in general dialogue from the very first step, and in M2 the wiki
is likewise mixed together with dialogue.

### 3.4 Byte-Specific Post-Training: Methods and Negative Lessons

LD3-base received no post-training of any kind. This section records the
methods and conclusions of a post-training chain built on top of it
(denoted M3); the weights of this chain have been deleted and only the
logs remain, and it does not enter the main table.

The trigger was an observation after deployment: 46% of LD3-base’s
self-generated answers contained 8-gram repetition (another commercial
model on the same questions: 6%), and it did not follow the writing
style guide written into the system prompt. Since prompting was
ineffective, the only remaining option was to train it in. M3’s goals,
in order of priority, were avoiding repetition, concise and correct
thinking, and working according to the style guide; the chain has four
steps, all on-policy:

1.  1.  Style-guide SFT: 10.5K style-guide general dialogues + about 5K
        style-guide logic problems (all correctly answered ones kept) + 4K
        replay, 16K window, lr 5e-6 with WSD, 259 steps.
2.  2.  Self-sampling with the decoding guard off: prompts are taken from
        the training pack as the prefix ”up to just before the last-turn
        answer”, 4 samples per prompt, official sampling parameters, 8,192
        bytes per sample cap. The decoding guard is turned off during
        sampling so that repetition is exposed; a sample cut off by the
        guard, once it enters the training data, teaches the model to write
        \</think\> in the answer segment.
3.  3.  Mining samples and RFT: clean = stopped on its own, contains
        \</think\>, 8-gram repetition rate $`\leq`$ 0.03, no whole-sentence
        repetition or stutter, style-lint score $`\geq`$ 80; bad = hitting
        the output cap, or repetition rate $`\geq`$ 0.10, or whole-sentence
        repetitions $`\geq`$ 2; for logic problems the chosen is ”correct
        with the shortest thinking”. Clean samples are first used for one
        round of RFT (lr 3e-6).
4.  4.  Length-normalized DPO: at most one pair per prompt, chosen = the
        clean sample with the highest lint score, rejected = the bad sample
        with the highest repetition rate. Reward r = $`\beta`$$`\cdot`$(log
        p $`-`$ log p_ref)/len, loss L = $`-`$log $`\sigma`$(r_c $`-`$ r_r
        $`-`$ $`\gamma`$) + $`\alpha`$$`\cdot`$($`-`$log p_c/len_c),
        $`\beta`$ 2.0 / $`\gamma`$ 0.5 / $`\alpha`$ 0.2, lr 5e-7. The
        normalization is necessary: in 99% of pairs the rejected is longer
        than the chosen (median lengths 634 vs 4,918 bytes).

Three rounds yielded three negative lessons:

- •
  Skipping RFT and going straight to DPO hurts precise reasoning. 61,600
  self-sampled responses, bad-sample rate 11.9%; direct DPO (4,460
  pairs, 140 steps) brought the bad-sample rate down to 7.7%, but greedy
  dialogue GSM8K on 300 problems dropped from 97.7% to 80.7%, and mean
  output length went from 1,198 to 3,681 tokens. (97.7% is under the
  protocol of the 300-problem greedy probe with thinking, not the
  protocol of the main table in Section 5.)
- •
  RFT before DPO brings it back. Adding a ”shortest and correct” RFT
  before DPO (7,004 pairs, 219 steps) brought GSM8K on 300 problems back
  to 92.7%.
- •
  Pushing repetition down further squeezes thinking out. In the
  third-round acceptance test the bad-sample rate was only 0.2%, but of
  252 answers with thinking, 211 had thinking shorter than 60
  characters, with a median of 28 characters, versus medians of 136 and
  210 in the first two rounds. Most of the 0.2% comes from ”not
  thinking”. The root cause is the pairing rule: taking the ”shortest”
  as chosen systematically selects samples without thinking; the rule
  was later changed so that the chosen’s thinking length is $`\geq`$ 1/4
  of the rejected’s, the thinking language is the same, and total
  lengths are as close as possible, so that a pair has no systematic
  difference other than the defect itself. Do not train when pairs are
  too few, either: a DPO on 218 pairs for 28 steps had pref_acc 0.375
  and repetition went up instead.

### 3.5 Deep-Draft MTP

A byte model emits one byte per step, so its number of decoding steps is
about 4$`\times`$ that of the original model; a multi-token prediction
(MTP) draft head is the main means of recovering speed. The Qwen3.5
family natively carries one MTP layer: fc\[5120, 10240\] concatenates
the next-token embedding with the backbone hidden state, followed by 1
full-attention decoder layer, sharing the embedding and lm_head with the
backbone (so the 384-entry vocabulary applies directly), 424.7M
parameters; once the backbone is trained, this layer has to be rebuilt
separately.

Draft depth is set by the number of Chinese characters, not the 2–3
steps customary for BPE models: a Chinese character is 3 bytes and the
continuation bytes within a character are nearly deterministic, so the
default is K=9 (3 characters), later raised to K=15 (5 characters);
training cost is $`\propto`$ K, but the MTP layer is only 1/64 of the
backbone. The head of LD3-base was trained with the backbone frozen and
only the head updated, K=15, 1,500 steps, lr 1e-4; after measurement, a
second round is triggered by ”fewer than 8 bytes accepted per round or
speedup below 1.5$`\times`$”, continuing on-policy on about 100 million
bytes (60,000 prompts) written by the model itself, lr 5e-5, keeping
whichever head has the higher acceptance length; the two rounds together
took about 35 GPU-hours.

Two pitfalls. First, the training-time metric and the serving-time
metric differ widely: the K=15 head on the pilot lines had a step-1 hit
rate of 0.935, yet in serving it accepted only 5.33 bytes per round and
was only 20% faster, because per-position accuracy decays from 0.93 to
0.40 at position 16. The head of LD3-base, running at K=8 on a single
GPU, accepts 5.7 bytes per round, giving 1.8$`\times`$ at 16 concurrent
streams and 3.3$`\times`$ single-stream (the configuration that could
not be re-measured on the single 48G GPU in Section 5.6). Second, once
the backbone changes, the old head is void and must be retrained;
multi-layer draft models and fine-tuning with a single-step objective
both fell short of the 1-layer MTP in our setting.

### 3.6 Decoding Guard

A byte model needs a layer of decoding guard that a BPE model does not;
the reasons are developed in Section 6. The guard is implemented as a
custom logit processor in the inference framework, with four components:

- •
  Thinking budget and answer budget: after \<think\>, force \</think\>
  when the budget is reached; after \</think\>, force \<\|im_end\|\> at
  the cap\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94even after the thought is
  closed, the answer segment can still loop up to the cap, so both
  segments need a budget. Serving default is 16,384 bytes for each.
- •
  UTF-8 validity mask: after a lead byte, only continuation bytes
  (128–191) are allowed; at a character boundary, bare continuation
  bytes and invalid lead bytes are forbidden.
- •
  Loop circuit breaker: force a close / end only when repetition is
  still ongoing after 1,024 consecutive steps; otherwise the logits are
  not modified. An early version forbade repetition byte by byte; on the
  pilot lines the gate was measured to be active on 41% of decoding
  steps (repeats within 16 bytes are common anyway in English, LaTeX and
  code), gaining in thinking mode and losing in non-thinking mode (GPQA
  thinking 48.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 60.6, non-thinking 60.6 $`\rightarrow`$
  53.0).

Two rules of use. First, the inference framework’s overlap scheduling
must be turned off: under overlap scheduling, the output the guard reads
lags by one token, so when the model has just emitted a lead byte the
guard still believes it is at a character boundary and forbids all legal
continuation bytes\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94the guard itself
manufactures the invalid UTF-8 it is meant to prevent; the
three-configuration comparison is given in Section 6.2. Second, there is
a ceiling on what the guard can recover: on the pilot lines, three guard
versions reduced ”no extractable answer” from 77 to 41–53 problems and
raised the close rate from 126 to 198/198, yet the number correct was
120/198 in every case (the original BPE model: 170); once the decoding
side has been squeezed dry, what remains is a capability gap. The guard
is therefore a net gain on tasks with ”thinking mode + a definite
answer”, while on tasks that demand long outputs with a specific
structure it cuts off structures that were not finished; the guard is
turned off when self-sampling training data (Section 3.4). The guard
used in the evaluation of Section 4 only blocks invalid byte sequences
and over-long outputs and does not change the distribution of legal
outputs.

## 4 Experimental Setup

### 4.1 Models and Checkpoints

Only two models are compared:

- •
  orig: the officially released Qwen3.8-27B (FP8 weights, block-128
  recipe), with a byte-level BPE vocabulary of 248,077 entries
  (embedding table of 248,320 rows).
- •
  LD3-base: the checkpoint obtained on the same backbone by shrinking
  the vocabulary to 384 (256 byte symbols + 128 special / reserved ids),
  reducing the embedding and output head from 1.27B parameters each to
  about 2M (language-model part 26.9B $`\rightarrow`$ 24.4B), and
  continuing training through the two-stage curriculum (Section 3.3),
  plus an MTP draft head of depth 8 (Section 3.5). Every table in this
  paper uses this single checkpoint; to align the protocol, it is also
  quantized to block-128 FP8 with the same recipe.

LD3-base has undergone no benchmark-oriented post-training; it is the
most direct answer to the question ”does byteification preserve the
original model’s ability”. Post-training problems specific to byte
models (repetition, greedy runaway) are discussed separately in Section
6 and do not enter the main table.

### 4.2 Training Compute

8$`\times`$H200, ZeRO-3 full-parameter continued training: M1 (encoding
stage) 47.5 h, M2 (reading stage, three segments combined) 131 h, 178.6
h in total for the backbone $`\approx`$ 1,430 GPU-hours; the MTP head
about 35 GPU-hours. 7.08 GB of bytes actually read, 4.77 GB of
supervised bytes (loss computed on assistant turns only). Corpus
generation is counted separately: self-generated general dialogue /
character dictionary / word dictionary / logic problems took about 760
GPU-hours on the local eight-GPU machine (from the generation queue
logs), and about 2,190 GPU-hours once external API calls are converted
and included (E3_E4.md). A rough 6ND estimate puts the backbone
continued training at about 1e21 FLOPs, the same order of magnitude as
Bolmo; an order of magnitude less data, but not less compute, so the
main text does not write ”N$`\times`$ cheaper”.

### 4.3 Evaluation Protocol (E1 / E2)

Both columns run every benchmark on the same RTX 6000 Ada 48G, with the
same serving stack (sglang v0.5.17, FP8, single GPU, no draft,
non-streaming, --disable-radix-cache), so that serving-side differences
are not counted as model differences. Specifically:

- •
  Two decoding modes: thinking mode temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95, with
  the content before \</think\> filtered out before scoring;
  non-thinking mode temperature 0. Both modes are controlled through the
  chat template’s enable_thinking switch; the template is identical to
  the official one.
- •
  Output caps aligned as bytes 4: the byte model’s cap is counted in
  bytes, and the BPE model gets 1/4 as many tokens (thinking mode 32,768
  B / 8,192 tok; non-thinking mode 16,384 B / 4,096 tok; LongBench-v2
  5,000 B / 1,250 tok). The measured median output-length ratio bytes /
  tokens is about 3 (footnote in Section 5.1), so the 4$`\times`$
  protocol is not tighter for the byte model.
- •
  Per-item counts accompany every score: the number of cap hits
  (stop_reason = max_tokens) and, in thinking mode, the number of items
  missing \</think\> are reported together, so that ”did not finish” is
  not conflated with ”cannot do it”.
- •
  Decoding guard: the byte model’s server carries a UTF-8 validity mask,
  byte budgets for thinking / answer, and a loop breaker (Section 3.6);
  the BPE model neither needs nor has one. The guard only blocks invalid
  byte sequences and over-long outputs; it does not change the
  distribution of valid outputs.
- •
  Datasets: the full GSM8K test set (1,319), MATH-500 (500), HumanEval+
  (164), IFEval (541 prompts / 834 instructions), C-Eval val (1,346),
  MMLU-Pro (72 questions sampled from each of 14 subjects, 1,008 in
  total), LongBench-v2 (the 117 questions that fit in the context).
  Scoring uses evalscope’s default scorers, the same code for both
  columns.
- •
  bpb: a held-out window set of 4 domains $`\times`$ 96 windows
  $`\times`$ 4,096 bytes; the byte model sums per-byte logprobs
  directly; the BPE model sums token logprobs and divides by the byte
  count of the same text.
- •
  Single seed, single run. For each item we give the per-item bootstrap
  95% interval and the paired $`\Delta`$ interval on the same questions
  (2,000 resamples, Appendix Table A2).

### 4.4 Character-Level Task Protocol (E5)

- •
  Test sets: CUTE (leukas/cute, 14 tasks, 400 questions sampled per
  task), the eng and zho languages of EXECUTE (benjamin/execute; 200
  questions per task), and our Chinese character suite of 15 tasks (200
  questions per task; traditional/simplified conversion 107 questions
  each, limited by the number of natural sentences that convert
  one-to-one). The character list for our suite is taken from the
  12,126-character common-use list; traditional/simplified facts from
  OpenCC STCharacters/TSCharacters (only one-to-one characters kept);
  pinyin / stroke count / radical from Unihan
  kMandarin/kTotalStrokes/kRSUnicode; natural sentences from C-Eval
  question stems (8–40 characters, no ASCII, $`\geq`$ 80% Chinese
  characters, 675 sentences in total). 13,214 questions in total after
  excluding extra\_\*.
- •
  Scoring: exact match. The ”答案:” (”Answer:”) prefix, leading/trailing
  quotes and the final period are stripped first, then whether
  whitespace is ignored is decided per task type; only the first
  non-empty paragraph of the response is taken. In thinking mode only
  the content after \</think\> is considered.
- •
  Decoding: non-thinking mode at temperature 0 is primary, and both
  columns run all test sets; thinking mode is run additionally only on
  all 14 CUTE tasks and our Chinese suite, 100 questions per task
  (temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95). Output cap 1,024 bytes / 256 tokens
  (thinking mode 16,384 bytes / 4,096 tokens).
- •
  Exclusions: the three extra\_\* splits of EXECUTE-zho (extra_c2g,
  extra_contains, extra_g2c, component description $`\leftrightarrow`$
  whole character) contain in the public data only inputs of the form
  ”Task: ⿰亻吏” with no task instruction (they were intended for
  few-shot use); both columns score 0 zero-shot, and they are not
  included in the tables. EXECUTE-zho therefore has 12 tasks, like eng.

### 4.5 Efficiency Protocol (E6)

Same GPU, same serving stack, four configurations: orig, orig + NEXTN
draft, LD3-base, LD3-base + NEXTN draft (K = 8). Three quantities: (1)
single-stream decoding, 10 Chinese and 10 English essay prompts of about
300 words, reported as Chinese characters per second and English
characters per second rather than tokens per second; (2) total
throughput at concurrency 16, likewise counted in characters; (3)
prefill: Chinese windows of 16,384 and 65,536 bytes, max_tokens = 1,
reporting time to first token (TTFT), median of 3 runs each. The draft
configurations need the memory fraction lowered to 0.80 and the context
lowered to 65,536 to start on a single GPU; a configuration that fails
to start is recorded as such (”does not start on a single GPU”).

## 5 Results

### 5.1 Main Table: How Much Byteification Preserved

Table 1 is the main result of this paper. Taking the two modes together:

- •
  Non-thinking mode (everyday usage): of the 7 items, GSM8K ($`-`$0.4),
  MATH-500 (+0.8), HumanEval+ ($`-`$2.5) and MMLU-Pro ($`-`$1.3) are
  within $`\pm`$2.5; C-Eval $`-`$4.7; the four IFEval metrics at
  $`-`$4.1 to $`-`$6.2 are the largest loss.
- •
  Thinking mode: MATH-500 (+1.4) and the four IFEval metrics (+0.2 to
  +0.6) are level or slightly higher, HumanEval+ $`-`$1.8, MMLU-Pro
  $`-`$1.3; GSM8K $`-`$4.0 and C-Eval $`-`$4.5 are the two clear losses.
- •
  The most consistent loss is on the Chinese exam (C-Eval about $`-`$4.5
  in both modes) and on instruction following in non-thinking mode; the
  most consistent preservation is on mathematics and MMLU-Pro. LD3-base
  has had no instruction-type post-training, and part of the
  non-thinking IFEval gap should be attributed to this (the same item is
  level in thinking mode), but this paper has no experiment that
  separates this factor.

### 5.2 Language Modeling: bpb

Table 2. All four domains are lower by about 2 standard errors, but the
window set is the held-out set from LD3 training, drawn from the same
distribution as its training data, which the original never saw, so this
cannot be read as stronger modeling ability; it only says that after
byteification the model returns to, and slightly below, the original’s
level on its own distribution; the zh_ood row is the most credible.
Figure 1 is the curve over the whole of training: the zero-adaptation
starting point (after vocabulary shrinking, before training) zh 3.02 /
zh_ood 3.29 / en 4.43 / code 2.54; at M1 step 100 en has already reached
0.58 while zh is still at 2.02; at the end of M1 zh 0.900 / zh_ood 1.213
/ en 0.575 / code 0.203; during M2 all four domains decline slowly and
monotonically, ending at 0.740 / 0.995 / 0.547 / 0.191. The training log
is computed on bf16 weights with CE calculated inside the trainer
process, whereas E2 uses FP8 weights with logprobs taken through the
server; the two readings of the same checkpoint differ by $`\leq`$
0.002, so Table 2 and Figure 1 can be read against each other. English
returns to the original’s level within the first 100 steps of M1,
whereas Chinese needed all 7 GB of bytes to catch
up\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94this is what Section 3.3’s ”Chinese
is the new skill” looks like in the loss.

### 5.3 Chinese

Chinese is what byteification is most likely to hurt, so two small probe
sets were used to watch it between M1 / M2, and a full-character
recitation was added at the end.

- •
  Five-way terminology probe. 12 Chinese–English terms (gradient
  descent, backpropagation, hash table, deadlock, etc.), each asked in 5
  ways: A English $`\rightarrow`$ Chinese, answer with the term only; B
  Chinese $`\rightarrow`$ English; C asked in Chinese, answered in
  Chinese; D asked in English with a Chinese answer required; E asked in
  Chinese with the English given in parentheses; greedy, with thinking,
  cap 8,192 bytes, answer section judged manually. At the end of M1: A
  0/12, B 6/12, C 6/12, D 11/12, E 12/12: the knowledge is there and the
  English pathway works; what is broken is the link between ”Chinese
  word form $`\leftrightarrow`$ concept”, which is direct evidence for
  Section 3.3’s ”Chinese is the new skill”. By M2 step 3,000, A is
  already 12/12 and B 10/12, unchanged thereafter.
- •
  30-question greedy probe. English 10 / Chinese 5 / code 5 / format 6 /
  gradient 4, temperature 0, cap 16,384 bytes, only the answer section
  after \</think\> is judged, and code questions are actually run
  against test cases. M1 29/30 $`\rightarrow`$ M2@3000 28
  $`\rightarrow`$ M2@6000 30 $`\rightarrow`$ LD3-base 30/30. Both probe
  sets are used only for decisions during training; n is too small for
  them to serve as main results.
- •
  Full-character recitation of 12,126 characters (E11). The character
  list shares its source with the character dictionary used in training
  (8,105 standard characters + 4,021 traditional characters); in groups
  of 20 (607 groups), the prompt asks the model to ”recite exactly,
  without missing a character”, greedy, non-thinking; the output is
  aligned character by character with the input, recording missing /
  wrong characters and invalid bytes; both columns on the same GPU under
  the same protocol, each run twice (dictionary order, then shuffled and
  regrouped). Over the two passes (24,252 character slots), orig gets 3
  characters wrong (汨 $`\rightarrow`$ 汩 and two rare characters copied
  as look-alikes) and LD3-base 1 (欽 copied as a look-alike that
  appeared earlier in the same group); all are copies of a neighboring
  or similar-looking character, none is missing; both columns have zero
  invalid UTF-8 and zero cap hits. Including the 4,021 traditional
  characters and rare characters from the extension blocks, the byte
  model writes characters byte by byte no worse than the original model;
  the difference is within noise.

- •
  Character operations lead across the board, with larger margins on
  Chinese than on English. On deleting / inserting / substituting /
  swapping characters, orthographic variants (orth) and finding
  characters, LD3-base leads by +10 to +43: CUTE sub_char 37.2
  $`\rightarrow`$ 71.2, ins_char 21.2 $`\rightarrow`$ 44.2; EXECUTE-zho
  swap_char 48.5 $`\rightarrow`$ 91.5, ins_char 65.5 $`\rightarrow`$
  99.5; our suite zh_swap_char 13.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 50.5, zh_del_char
  62.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 94.5, zh_sub_char 53.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 85.5.
  Word-level operations (del_word / ins_word / sub_word / contains_word)
  are already near-perfect in both columns and stay level.
- •
  Not achieved by writing more. The byte model’s output byte count is
  about 2–4$`\times`$ the original’s token count, consistent with the
  sequence-length ratio; cap hits are close to 0 in both columns. The
  original only gets these items right in thinking mode (CUTE 75.2
  $`\rightarrow`$ 89.4, our suite 54.4 $`\rightarrow`$ 87.8), at a cost
  of hundreds to thousands of tokens per item (CUTE del_word averages
  3,306 tokens, 36/100 cap hits).
- •
  The byte model drops on Chinese character knowledge tasks.
  zh_homophone (pick the homophone among four choices) 96.5
  $`\rightarrow`$ 57.5, zh_strokes 63.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 47.0, zh_pinyin
  98.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 91.5; zh_radical +5.0 and traditional/simplified
  conversion +1.9 are level. Giving the pinyin of a single character is
  still acceptable, but comparing the pronunciations of four characters
  clearly is not: of the 85 wrong answers, 71 chose A (defaulting to the
  first option when unsure). Pronunciation and stroke count are
  ”character $`\rightarrow`$ attribute” lookup knowledge; after
  byteification the 3 bytes of each Chinese character must be relearned,
  and this knowledge has not fully come
  back\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94the same direction as C-Eval
  $`-`$4.5 in Section 5.1. This is the point this section most needs to
  state honestly: byteification buys operational ability at the cost of
  part of the character-level knowledge.
- •
  Counting and positioning are weak in both columns. On zh_count /
  zh_nth / zh_index / zh_reverse the original scores 6–23 and the byte
  model 25–37; under non-thinking greedy decoding neither 27B model
  counts positions reliably, and byteification merely errs a little
  less.
- •
  Excluded tasks: EXECUTE-zho extra_c2g / extra_contains / extra_g2c
  carry no task instructions (Section 4.4); orig 63.5 / 0 / 0, LD3-base
  15.5 / 0 / 0, not included in the tables.

In thinking mode (100 items per task, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95, cap
16,384 bytes / 4,096 tokens) both columns are near-perfect and the gap
narrows to CUTE +1.9 and our suite +1.3, but the per-task breakdown
still has structure:

- •
  The byte model is still higher on character operations, by +4 to +34:
  zh_reverse 59 $`\rightarrow`$ 93, swap_word 77 $`\rightarrow`$ 96,
  zh_swap_char 84 $`\rightarrow`$ 98, ins_char 85 $`\rightarrow`$ 95; on
  the four Chinese counting / positioning tasks the byte model scores
  100 / 100 / 100 / 93 (original 93 / 96 / 95 / 59).
- •
  Thinking does not recover the Chinese character knowledge tasks:
  stroke count 34 vs 69, pinyin 88 vs 99, homophone 88 vs 99, radical 64
  vs 72\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94lookup knowledge is not
  something reasoning can make up for.
- •
  Two tasks where the byte model instead drops: CUTE del_word 64
  $`\rightarrow`$ 56 and orth 67 $`\rightarrow`$ 48, caused by cap hits
  (43/100 and 53/100, original 36 / 33), with an average output of about
  10,000 bytes. On a supplementary re-sampling run the cap-hit count
  rose further, indicating a probabilistic case of the thought never
  closing rather than a few specific items. This is direct evidence for
  the byte-model-specific problems of Section 6, and the reason the
  thinking-mode conclusions are less clean than the non-thinking ones.

Per-task thinking-mode results are in Appendix Table A1. Figure 2 plots
the $`\Delta`$ of Table 4 per task, with operation and knowledge tasks
in different colors.

### 5.5 Long Context

LD3-base’s training windows are only 64K (M1) and 16K (M2) bytes; the
positional encoding was left untouched and no dedicated long-position
training was done. This section asks how much of the original’s
long-context ability remains after byteification. All four items are
measured on LD3-base, without an original-model comparison (on the same
suites the original left only a record of ”no drop up to 1M”, with no
scores), so they demonstrate retention only and make no comparison.

- •
  Held-out bpb at 128k: 0.257 (0–8k bucket 0.196, 64–128k bucket 0.268):
  95 held-out long sessions, one forward pass over the full 128k-byte
  window, per-position CE computed only on assistant segments, bucketed
  by target position. This window set is not the same as the four-domain
  windows of Section 5.2, and the two are not comparable.
- •
  Needle test 8k–128k, 4/4 throughout: our own documents are
  concatenated into a haystack, a one-line ”project id $`\rightarrow`$
  passphrase” memo is inserted at depth 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the question is
  asked at the end, greedy decoding, hit = the passphrase appears.
- •
  Ordering probe 16k–128k, 6/6 throughout: two memos placed 0.3 / 0.6
  apart, asked ”which one appears first”.
- •
  Up to 1M bytes: our own 8 task types (needle, verbatim transcription,
  hex / base64 / URL encoding and decoding, two-hop, summation,
  ordering, long-document reading), 46 items per length tier, with the
  evidence at the beginning and the question at the end, tiers differing
  only in padding length; greedy decoding with thinking, cap 16,384
  bytes, only the answer segment is scored. With static YaRN
  $`\times`$4.5 enabled, LD3-base scores 256K 39, 512K 35, 768K 37, 1M
  33/46; without YaRN, 1M 27/46; the errors are mostly in the
  encoding/decoding types.

The conclusion is one sentence: at positions 2–64$`\times`$ beyond the
training window the model can still read and locate, the original’s
positional ability survives byteification, and length extrapolation can
simply reuse the original’s YaRN. The LongBench-v2 row of E1 is
dominated by the output cap and is not used as long-context evidence
(Section 5.1 footnote).

computation per step but in less output per step. Table 5 reports
measurements on the same RTX 6000 Ada 48G with the same serving stack
(single-stream: mean over 10 prompts per language; concurrency 16;
prefill: median of 3 runs; protocol of Section 4.5).

  Identical per-step speed. Single-stream token/s is nearly the same in

  307). The entire difference is in output per step: for the original, 1
  token $`\approx`$ 1.45 Chinese characters or 5.0 English characters;
  for the byte model, 1 step = 1 byte $`\approx`$ 0.32 Chinese
  characters or 1 English character. Hence both Chinese characters per

  original, and the ratio is unchanged under concurrency.
- •
  Prefill loses more. For the same 65,536-byte Chinese input, the
  original has about 20,000 tokens and the byte model 65,622 tokens;
  time to first token goes 4.52 $`\rightarrow`$ 29.57 s (6.5$`\times`$),
  twice the token-count ratio (about 3.2). The excess is an engineering
  gap: the byte model runs through add-on chunked GDN and attention
  kernels that lack the tuning of the BPE path. This is not a property
  of the model itself, but it is the current state.
- •
  The draft head does not fit on a single 48G GPU. Neither NEXTN
  configuration starts (with the 27B FP8 weights plus the draft head,
  the KV pool no longer fits), so Table 5 has no draft rows. The
  evidence that MTP is especially effective for the byte model can only
  be cited from records on other hardware: with K = 8, about 5.7 bytes
  accepted per round, about 3.3$`\times`$ single-stream and about
  1.8$`\times`$ at concurrency 16. Scaled accordingly, single-stream
  Chinese characters per second would return to 0.7–0.8$`\times`$ the
  original and to about 0.4$`\times`$ under

  throughput on the same hardware remains below the original.
- •
  One more number under the end-to-end protocol: the wall-clock time for
  all E1 benchmarks in both modes on the same GPU is orig 7 h 44 min and
  LD3-base 35 h 57 min (4.6$`\times`$), consistent with the individual
  ratios in Table 5.

### 5.7 Multilingual (E11)

The continued training of LD3-base used Chinese and English data only
(Section 3.2). This section uses a smoke test of 22 languages $`\times`$
3 items to see how much of the ”byte channel” and of the generation
ability remain, both columns on the same GPU under the same protocol
(E11): (1) recite a sentence in the language verbatim
(character-by-character comparison after NFC normalization); (2)
translate the same Chinese sentence into the language; (3) ask a
capital-city common-knowledge question in the language and require an
answer in that language; greedy, one run without thinking (caps 512 /
512 / 1,024) and one with thinking (4,096 / 4,096 / 8,192), with the
same max_tokens values for both columns (for the BPE model this amounts
to about 3–4$`\times`$ the text budget, so the original model’s numbers
are an upper bound). Translation and QA are scored automatically: the
fraction of letters in the output that fall in the target script
(script_match), 8-gram repetition rate and cap hits to detect loops, and
whether the QA answer contains the gold string; kept = translation and
answer both have script_match $`\geq`$ 0.9 and do not loop, degraded =
either item loops or has script_match ¡ 0.5, marginal = the rest.

| --------------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---- | -------- | -------- |
| orig non-thinking     | 22/22      | 22/22      | 21   | 1        | 0        |
| orig thinking         | 21/22      | 22/22      | 22   | 0        | 0        |
| LD3-base non-thinking | 22/22      | 13/22      | 11   | 0        | 11       |
| LD3-base thinking     | 22/22      | 14/22      | 13   | 0        | 9        |

表 6: 22-language smoke test (E11; recitation = number of languages
recited exactly, QA = number answered correctly, kept / marginal /
degraded = number of languages per automatic tier by script and looping)

Reading:

- •
  The byte channel is intact; generation splits by script. Recitation is
  nearly perfect in both columns (in thinking mode the original model
  repeats tone marks in one Thai sentence, a BPE token-boundary artifact
  on Thai; the byte model is 22/22). In generation the original model
  keeps all 22 languages; the byte model keeps only the major Latin- and
  Cyrillic-script languages plus Japanese (11 in non-thinking mode:
  Russian, Japanese, Arabic, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese,
  Vietnamese, Turkish, Polish, Italian), while non-Latin scripts such as
  Greek, Korean, Persian, the Indic languages, Thai and Hebrew degrade:
  translations loop or become word salad, and QA answers miss the
  question (in Hindi it says the capital of India is ”Hindi”).
- •
  The degradation is a data problem, not an architectural one. Intact
  copying shows the byte channel is not broken; what is missing is
  supervised bytes in these languages, as the two-stage curriculum
  contains only Chinese and English (Section 3.2). Bringing them back
  would require mixing the corresponding languages into the
  continued-training data, which this paper did not do.
- •
  Thinking is double-edged for low-resource scripts. With thinking on,
  Greek, Korean, Ukrainian and Indonesian move from degraded back to
  kept (the translation is written out in one go); Vietnamese, Swahili
  and Arabic drop instead, in every case because the thinking itself
  loops in that language up to the cap and the body is empty; the net
  effect is +2 languages (11 $`\rightarrow`$ 13), at 1,356 s against 171
  s for the original model. This is the same phenomenon as ”the thought
  never closes” in Sections 5.4 and 6.1.

## 6 Failure Modes Specific to Byte Models

Spreading one BPE token over about 4 bytes amounts to splitting every
sampling decision into 4. The four problems below all stem from this;
they do not exist, or are not serious, in BPE models, and must be
handled separately in byte models.

### 6.1 Runaway under Greedy Decoding

Phenomenon. At temperature 0 the byte model may write all the way to the
output cap without closing. In one non-thinking GPQA-Diamond greedy
evaluation on the pilot lines, 34 of 198 items (17%) filled the
16,384-byte cap with no answer line; the BPE original built on the same
weights had 0 items with no extractable answer under greedy decoding,
with an output p90 of only 2,005 characters. In the thinking-mode greedy
evaluation of the first-round 27B byteification, 42% of IFEval samples
hit the 32,768-byte cap. On LD3-base the same phenomenon appears in the
thinking-mode character-level tasks: in CUTE del_word and orth, 43/100
and 53/100 samples respectively hit the 16,384-byte cap; whereas on the
seven benchmarks of the main table in Section 5, the number of LD3-base
thinking-mode cap hits is no higher than the original’s on every item,
so this is a problem of particular task types, not a general ”thinking
that never stops”.

Cause. Runaway samples split into two kinds: half are byte-level
infinite loops (\end{bmatrix} repeated endlessly, consecutive newlines,
60-character-block repetition rate $`\geq`$ 0.9), and half are ”Let me
reconsider\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”A6
Actually\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”A6” thoughts that never finish
(repetition rate $`\approx`$ 0). The former is the greedy chain locking
into a cycle more easily at the byte level: each Chinese character takes
3 steps, each step’s argmax is near-deterministic, and once it enters a
high-probability short cycle there is no randomness to bring it out. The
latter is long-range closing never having been supervised: end symbols
are all counted in the loss, but no training window ends with a
loss-bearing end symbol, so once thinking exceeds the p99 length the
model has never seen ”time to
stop”\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94this is exposure bias,
essentially a problem of the RL domain.

Fix. Three measures that leave the model untouched: always sample rather
than decode greedily in evaluation and serving; align the output cap
with BPE models at bytes 4 (Section 4.3); report the counts of ”no
extractable answer / cap hits / unjudgeable” alongside scores, because
”counting no extractable answer as wrong” turns all such samples into
inability. To these is added the decoding guard of Section 3.6 (budget +
circuit breaker). The measure that changes the model is the
self-sampling RFT of Section 3.4.

Evidence. After the pilot lines switched from greedy to sampling, GPQA
items with no extractable answer fell 34 $`\rightarrow`$ 24 and the
score rose 54.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 60.6; adding the guard, thinking mode
went 48.0 $`\rightarrow`$ 60.6. But the number of correct answers for
all three guard versions stopped at 120/198 (the original BPE model:
170): the decoding side can only turn ”unfinished” into ”finished”;
whether the finished output is correct depends on the model.

### 6.2 Byte-wise Sampling Breaks UTF-8

Phenomenon. With sampling on, symbols that should not appear
occasionally show up in the output: in samples the multiplication sign
became a geometric-shape symbol, and a superscript symbol became a
currency symbol (both are valid characters sharing the same lead byte as
the original character but with a different continuation byte). The
worse case is producing an invalid byte sequence outright, which the
decoding end can only display as the replacement character.

Cause. The three bytes of a Chinese character or symbol are one sampling
decision in a BPE model and three in a byte model. After the lead byte,
at temperature 0.7 there is still a small probability of sampling
another valid continuation byte (valid but wrong) or a non-continuation
byte (invalid sequence). The former is an inherent cost of byte
sampling; the latter can be eliminated on the decoding side.

Fix. Add a UTF-8 validity mask on the decoding side (Section 3.6). The
mask depends on the state ”the byte just sampled”, so the inference
framework’s overlap scheduling must be turned off: otherwise the output
the guard reads lags by one token, and when a lead byte has just been
emitted the guard still believes it is at a character boundary and
instead bans all valid continuation bytes, turning the output into
”lead, lead, continuation” triples. The ”valid but wrong” garbling can
only be handled by tightening sampling; the mask cannot cure it.

Evidence. This bug was found on a pilot-line checkpoint: for the same
Chinese prompt, with the guard on + overlap scheduling the output was
almost entirely replacement characters without a single complete Chinese
character; with the guard fully off there were occasional invalid
sequences; with the guard on + overlap scheduling off the output was
entirely valid. It once led us to believe the model had not learned
Chinese encoding; all historical scores obtained with the guard were
therefore re-examined.

### 6.3 Presence / Frequency Penalties Are Ineffective on a 256-Entry Vocabulary

Phenomenon. The common remedy for repetition is to turn on presence /
frequency penalty. After deployment, LD3-base reproduced repetition on
real agent inputs (16,000-token prefix), and adding a frequency /
presence penalty had no effect.

Cause. Both penalties keep accounts per token id, lowering ids that have
already appeared. In a 150,000-entry vocabulary ”has appeared” is
informative; among 256 bytes every common byte has appeared within a few
steps, so the penalty amounts to shifting all bytes together and cannot
suppress n-gram-level loops. Repetition suppression for byte models must
be done at the n-gram level, for which inference frameworks have no
ready-made implementation.

Fix. On the decoding side, use the n-gram-level loop detection of
Section 3.6, but feed it only to the circuit breaker and leave the
logits untouched otherwise\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94byte-wise
repetition banning would falsely trigger on 41% of decoding steps in
normal text. On the training side, use the on-policy RFT / DPO of
Section 3.4.

Evidence. See the guard results in Section 6.1 and the training results
in Section 6.4; the penalties themselves have no positive number to
report.

### 6.4 Repetition and Its Treatment

Phenomenon. 46% of LD3-base’s self-generated answers contain 8-gram
repetition; on the same prompts another commercial model has 6% and
another open-source model 13%. Chinese thinking repetition under long
context (24–32K prefix) is a probabilistic event: the original
Qwen3.8-27B on the same long Chinese task also repeated 2 times out of
10 samples (20%), and 0/3 when sampled 3 times. Under a stricter
criterion (loops / whole-sentence repetition) the rate is only 4–6%; the
two numbers are not directly comparable.

Cause. Three layers. First, the byte level amplifies exposure bias by
about 4$`\times`$, and once in a short cycle there is no randomness to
bring it out (Section 6.1). Second, the original model already has some
probability of repeating itself while thinking; after byteification
Chinese supervised bytes are fewer (see Section 3.2), so the repetition
rate of Chinese thinking is higher. Third, part of the ”stutter” is not
the model’s illness: the ”你你好” and ”感感文件” seen in client-side
streaming are caused by the inference framework’s incremental
detokenization computing offsets by character count and re-sending text
when the three steps of one Chinese character arrive on a byte
vocabulary; the non-streaming output of the same request is clean, and
the stutter rate is only 0.2–0.5%.

Fix. Prompting is ineffective (LD3-base ignores the style guide written
into the system prompt), penalties are ineffective (Section 6.3), so it
can only be trained in: Section 3.4’s self-sampling (guard off)
$`\rightarrow`$ RFT $`\rightarrow`$ length-normalized DPO. The pairing
rule determines what DPO learns: between chosen and rejected there must
be no systematic difference other than the ”illness” (length, amount of
thinking, thinking language). Verifying repetition requires $`\geq`$ 10
samples and reporting the trigger rate.

Evidence. On the M3 chain the bad-sample rate (repetition / stutter /
cap hits) went 11.9% $`\rightarrow`$ 7.7% (direct DPO) $`\rightarrow`$
0.2% (RFT + two rounds of DPO); the cost was precise reasoning: GSM8K
300-item greedy dialogue 97.7% $`\rightarrow`$ 80.7%, and RFT before DPO
recovered it to 92.7%. But the 0.2% must be discounted: in the last
round, 211 of 252 thinking answers had thoughts shorter than 60
characters, median 28 characters; most of it comes from ”not thinking”.
Long-context repetition has its own conclusions: SFT works (200 clean
long prefixes brought the trigger rate on the long Chinese task from 20%
$`\rightarrow`$ 0%; 513 Chinese 32K items brought repetition on English
agent inputs from 2/10 $`\rightarrow`$ 1/10), while DPO with too few
pairs does not (169 pairs and 218 pairs, one run each). Up to LD3-base,
repetition has not been cured; this is one of the limitations in Section 7.

## 7 Limitations

- •
  Single seed, single run. The decoding randomness of thinking-mode
  sampling at 0.6 was not measured; the bootstrap intervals cover only
  item-sampling variance.
- •
  The bpb comparison shares the distribution of the training data
  (Section 5.2): it cannot be read as stronger modeling ability.
- •
  The attribution of the non-thinking IFEval gap is unclear: LD3-base
  has had no instruction-type post-training whereas the original has;
  this paper has no experiment isolating this factor.
- •
  Efficiency is a real cost: Chinese characters per second on the same
  GPU is about 1/4 of the original, and long-input prefill is
  5–6.5$`\times`$ slower; the draft head could not be measured on a
  single GPU, and only data from elsewhere can be cited.
- •
  Character-level knowledge is not fully recovered: lookup knowledge of
  the ”character $`\rightarrow`$ attribute” kind, such as pronunciation
  / stroke count, drops after byteification, in the same direction as
  the C-Eval loss; this paper does not answer how much Chinese data
  would be needed to recover it.
- •
  Thinking mode is unstable: without post-training, the byte model
  cannot find its way out of thinking on some task types (del_word /
  orth in Section 5.4); the treatment is in Sections 3.4 / 6.4, but the
  treated model is outside the comparison scope of this paper.
- •
  Multilingual degradation (Section 5.7): generation in non-Latin /
  non-Cyrillic scripts degrades (11–13/22 languages kept against
  21–22/22 for the original model) while recitation is intact; only 3
  items per language were tested, so this is a smoke test rather than a
  benchmark, and using the same max_tokens values for both columns gives
  the original model 3–4$`\times`$ the text budget.
- •
  The vision tower was not re-adapted; long-context repetition is not
  cured; some conclusions (the quantification of greedy runaway, the
  ineffectiveness of penalties) come from the pilot lines rather than
  LD3 itself, as noted in the text.
- •
  Contamination between evaluation and training sets was not
  systematically checked (C-Eval question stems were used as natural
  sentences in our Chinese character suite, but both models had already
  been evaluated on them in E1, and the character tasks do not test
  knowledge).

## 8 Conclusion

Converting a 27B subword model as is into a pure byte model is feasible:
vocabulary 248,320 $`\rightarrow`$ 384, backbone untouched, 4.77 GB of
supervised bytes, about 1,430 H200 GPU-hours, and most of the original’s
ability is retained\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94math, code and
MMLU-Pro are within noise, while Chinese exams and non-thinking
instruction following drop 4–6 points. What byteification buys is
character-level manipulation ability that does not rely on thinking
(especially pronounced for Chinese); what it costs is character
throughput on the same hardware (down to 1/4–1/5 of the original) and
part of the lookup knowledge of Chinese characters. Byte models also
bring a set of failure modes of their own, which have corresponding
engineering and training fixes. For those who want to try byteification
on an existing model, our advice is threefold: use the target model’s
own output for dialogue-type supervision; put the dictionary (explicit
character $`\leftrightarrow`$ byte supervision) first in the curriculum;
at evaluation time, align the output cap at bytes 4 and record cap-hit
counts per item.

一字节一 token:用模型自产语料把 27B 混合注意力模型改造成纯字节模型

张栗伟(Liwei Zhang)  童志明(ZhiMing Tong)

澜砥实验室(Landi Lab)

z@metiy.xyz  mynameistong@163.com

2026 年 11 月

本文为同一篇论文的中文版;英文版在前(第 1
页起)。两版实验与数字完全一致,参考文献见英文版末。

## 附录 1 引言

子词分词器是训练前冻结的设计决定。对中文,Qwen3.8 的 byte-level BPE
在中文维基上平均 3.84 字节 / token,64% 的 token
是单字(tokenizer-eval/),一个词常被切成几个碎片;对所有语言,拼写、字符位置、数字的各位对模型都不可见,字符级操作要靠”思考”把词拆开再做(5.4
节)。词表一旦定下,后面所有的训练与服务都绑在它上面。

最直接的替代是字节模型:1 字节 = 1 token,词表 256
加特殊符号。从零训一个字节模型太贵;已有的两条现实路线各有代价\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94保留切块结构(局部编码器 +
补丁,BLT、Bolmo),模型主干看到的仍是切块后的向量;或经字节接口做跨分词器蒸馏(1B–8B
上仍被判为开放问题)。本文走第三条路:把一个已训好的 27B
子词模型,原样改成不切块的纯字节模型,只换词表与嵌入,主干一字不改。

我们的做法是:词表收缩到 384(BPE 词表里本来就有 256
个字节符号),然后用两段课程续训\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94先用字典、词典、对话学”字
$`\leftrightarrow`$ 字节”的编码,再读人写的百科原文(3 节)。对话 /
行为类监督全部由原版 Qwen3.8 自己生成(on-policy
自蒸馏,按轮独立补答、只监督本轮),知识阅读用人写原文(占监督字节
54%)。监督 4.77 G 字节,8$`\times`$H200 178.6 h。

本文想回答的只有四个问题,也是四点贡献:

1.  1.  保住了多少(5.1、5.2):同卡、同服务栈、同解码口径的两列对照。非思考档
        7 项里 4 项在配对自助法区间内看不出差别,C-Eval 与非思考档 IFEval 掉
        4–6 分;思考档 GSM8K $`-`$4.0、C-Eval $`-`$4.5。
2.  2.  字节带来了什么(5.4):不开思考时字符级操作全面领先(CUTE
        +8.8、EXECUTE-zho +12.2、自建中文题
        +9.7),中文幅度大于英文;但汉字的读音 /
        笔画等查表知识掉了,思考也补不回。
3.  3.  代价是什么(5.6):每步速度相同,每步产出少 3–5 倍;同卡汉字 / 秒降到
        1/4,64K 字节 prefill 慢 6.5$`\times`$;草稿头是补回的路,但 48G
        单卡装不下。
4.  4.  字节模型特有的失效模式与修法(6 节):贪心跑飞、按字节采样打断
        UTF-8、惩罚项对小词表无效、思考绕不出来;以及对应的护栏与后训练方法。

我们不声称字节模型更强。诚实的结论是:在 27B 规模、约 1e21 FLOPs
的续训预算下,不切块的字节化可以追平原版的大部分能力,换来字符级操作的收益,付出吞吐与一部分字级知识的代价。评测脚本、自建中文字符题集与本文全部评测的判分
/ 自助法代码公开于
https://huggingface.co/datasets/leiwhere/ld3-byte-eval;权重与训练语料暂不发布。

## 附录 2 相关工作

从零训练的字节 / 字符模型。 ByT5 \[[25](#bib.bib25)\] 把 T5 直接喂 UTF-8
字节,是”扁平字节”的早期代表;CANINE \[[3](#bib.bib3)\] 与 Charformer
\[[22](#bib.bib22)\] 用下采样或可微的软子词把字符序列压短;MEGABYTE
\[[28](#bib.bib28)\]、SpaceByte \[[21](#bib.bib21)\]、BLT
\[[14](#bib.bib14)\] 与 H-Net \[[10](#bib.bib10)\]
把”切块”做进架构\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94固定长、按空格、按熵或端到端学出的边界,再在块上跑主干。MambaByte
\[[23](#bib.bib23)\] 与 EvaByte \[[31](#bib.bib31)\]
保持扁平字节,但分别换成 SSM 主干或从零训练
6.5B。这些工作都从零训练;本文的出发点不同:一个已经花费数十万亿 token
训好的子词模型,能否不重训主干、不加切块结构,直接改成字节模型。

把子词模型改成字节模型。 BLT 报告了用 Llama 3.1 8B 初始化全局
Transformer 的实验(220B token),保留 patching 与新训的局部编解码器
\[[14](#bib.bib14)\]。Bolmo \[[13](#bib.bib13)\] 系统地做了这件事:Olmo 3
7B 改成字节级”潜分词器语言模型”,字节池化成 patch、mLSTM
局部编解码器,两阶段共约 49B token(第二阶段 39.3B);同样保留切块,主干按
patch 运行。[Bao et al. \[1\]](#bib.bib1) 用渐进蒸馏把 token
老师的表示对齐到 H-Net 式层级字节学生($`\leq`$ 4B)。[Singh et al.
\[20\]](#bib.bib20)
只把字节当作跨分词器蒸馏的接口,学生仍是子词模型,并报告 1B–8B
上一致收益”仍难以获得”。推理期方法 \[[9](#bib.bib9)\] 不训练,把任意 BPE
模型变成字节级采样器,模型内部仍按子词计算。与它们相比,本文(i)完全不切块,主干对每个字节各算一步;(ii)不引入外部老师,监督来自原模型自己的输出与人写原文;(iii)规模
27B、以中文为重点,并给出同卡的效率代价。不切块的代价是序列长度不压缩,5.6
节如实报告。

词表迁移。 ZeTT \[[12](#bib.bib12)\]、FOCUS \[[5](#bib.bib5)\]、TokAlign
\[[11](#bib.bib11)\] 研究换一套子词 tokenizer
时如何初始化新嵌入、少步数恢复。本文是其极端情形:新词表只剩 256
个字节符号,而这 256 行本就在原嵌入表中(GPT-2 式字节级 BPE
\[[18](#bib.bib18)\]),所以不需要任何初始化技巧,困难全部转移到续训。

自生成数据与 on-policy。 Self-Instruct \[[24](#bib.bib24)\]、STaR
\[[30](#bib.bib30)\] 与 RFT \[[29](#bib.bib29)\]
用模型自己(过滤后)的输出训自己;SDFT \[[27](#bib.bib27)\]
让种子模型改写任务答案以缓解遗忘;[Chen et al. \[2\]](#bib.bib2) 把 RL
少遗忘归因于 on-policy 数据。本文的语料配方(3.2 节)与后训练(3.4
节)建立在同一观察上\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94对话类监督必须是目标模型自己当前的输出\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94并把它用在词表替换这个分布剧变的设定下;DPO
\[[19](#bib.bib19)\] 用作复读治理的手段,带长度归一化。

底座与基准。 Qwen3.8-27B \[[17](#bib.bib17)\] 是 Gated DeltaNet
\[[26](#bib.bib26)\] 与全注意力按 3:1 混合的稠密模型(同系架构说明见
\[[16](#bib.bib16), [15](#bib.bib15)\]),原生带一层 MTP \[[8](#bib.bib8),
[4](#bib.bib4)\]。字符级任务用 CUTE \[[6](#bib.bib6)\] 与其多语种扩展
EXECUTE \[[7](#bib.bib7)\]。

## 附录 3 方法

### 3.1 词表收缩

Qwen3.8-27B 的分词器是 GPT-2 式的字节级 BPE(byte-level
BPE):词表里本来就有 256 个单字节符号,所有多字节 token
都由它们合并而来。改成纯字节模型因此不需要新建任何嵌入,只需删掉全部合并项,保留
256 个字节行和对话模板依赖的特殊符号。收缩后的词表是 384 项:字节 0–255
按字节值排,随后是
\<\|endoftext\|\>=256、\<\|im_start\|\>=257、\<think\>=280 等 35
个命名特殊符号,其余 93 个位置是占位(全表见附录 B)。tokenizer 里没有任何
merge 规则,一个 UTF-8 字节就是一个 token。

主干一字不改:64 层 = 48 层 GatedDeltaNet + 16 层全注意力(每 4
层一个),hidden 5120,model_type 仍是
qwen3_5,现成推理框架直接装载。参数只在两端变化:嵌入与 lm_head 各从
248,320 $`\times`$ 5,120 $`\approx`$ 1.27B 缩到 384 $`\times`$ 5,120
$`\approx`$ 2M,语言模型部分从 26.9B 变成 24.4B;视觉塔 0.46B
原样冻结。收缩脚本按 token 名字取行而不按 id 偏移;产物用特殊 id
表与对话模板的 md5 逐项核对(两处容易漏的错误:config 里的视觉 token
id、新版 transformers 对特殊符号的重排)。

代价是序列变长:原分词器在中文上 3.84 字节/token、英文
4.35,字节版序列约为原来的 4 倍,16K 字节窗大致相当于 BPE 的 4k
token。中文文本里只有 15.9%(数字、标点、换行)本来就落在单字节 token
上,99.4%
的汉字在原模型里从不走字节路径,所以零适应的模型能读却读不好:未训练的收缩检查点四域
bpb 为 zh 3.02 / en 4.43 / code
2.54。这组数只用来检验收缩没做错(与第一轮 27B
试点的零适应数同量级),不当作起点能力的度量。

### 3.2 语料:对话类监督自产,知识阅读用人写的原文

LD3-base 两段课程共读入 7.08 G 字节、受监督 4.77 G
字节。监督字节按来源分:wiki 原文 2.56 G(54%)、词典 1.61 G(34%)、字典
0.30 G(6%)、一般对话 0.16 G、编码会话 0.14 G。要先说清楚:占监督字节 54%
的 wiki
是人类写的维基百科原文,按预训练方式首尾相接切窗读入,不是模型自产;自产的是其余四类对话
/ 行为类监督。原文负责知识阅读,自产对话负责”模型用字节说自己的话”。

对话类监督全部由原版 Qwen3.8-27B
自己生成(on-policy),依据是两组对照。Ornith
试点线的六个”少思考”训练对照里,只有模型自己当前的输出训自己是零代价(自己的正确样本训
3.2 遍,正确率 49% 不动),四个用别人写的数据的配方全部掉 5–14
分,与内容好坏无关;”当前”严格到差一个训练阶段就不算。跨词表蒸馏的三臂对照指向同一件事:监督别人写的提示词前缀让
code bpb 变差 26%、en 变差 16%,限制到本轮生成后损伤消失。所以本文 CE
只算助手轮(含思考);多轮会话按轮独立补答,前缀原样保留,只监督本轮。

四类自产语料:(1)字典,12,126 个汉字(8,105 个规范字 + 4,021
个简繁写法不同的繁体字),读音、义项、简繁关系取自 Unihan / CC-CEDICT /
OpenCC,每字三轮对话(条目 $`\rightarrow`$ 整条译成另一语言
$`\rightarrow`$ 追问);它是”字 $`\leftrightarrow`$
三个字节”最直接的显式监督,所以排第一。(2)词典,141,361 个词条种子
$`\times`$ 4
轮。字典与词典的写法规则是”事实来自词典,文字由老师写”:提示是自然对话,格式要求只放在不受监督的用户轮,人设摊开成
33 种以免文风被单一人设带偏。(3)一般对话,六个公开会话池去重后 60,549
段、共 113 万个助手轮,其中 91% 是带工具调用的 agent
轮。(4)真人编码会话,两个公开数据集(6,772 段 + 1,064 段)按轮补答两遍共
88,743 轮。全部生成开思考、用官方采样参数(temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 20)。

生成量远大于训练用量:一般对话本机生成了 30 多万轮,进入课程的监督字节只有
0.16 G,因为前缀长、只监督末轮。本机生成合计约 94.9 h $`\approx`$ 760
H200 GPU 时;走托管接口的部分(作文 2,048 篇、逻辑题约 11,800
道、编码会话)算力不可见,只报调用量。作文与逻辑题没有进入 LD3-base
的两段课程:逻辑题(reasoning-gym 99 类,10,560 道、答对 9,618 道)用在 3.4
节,作文(两批共约 2,560 篇)只生成、未入任何训练包。

### 3.3 两段课程:先学编码,再读书

训练一律全参、ZeRO-3,检查点只存权重(47
GB);两段都用常数学习率,段间仅权重续训(优化器重置、5 步预热),实测 bpb
无回退。决策同时看四域字节 bpb、30
题贪心探针和对话留出集,单看任一个都不做决定。

M1 编码阶段(64K 字节窗,2,077 步,lr 3e-6,47.5 h):字典 : 词典 :
一般对话按监督字节 1:1:1
混合,字典全量一遍,词典按字覆盖抽样,一般对话只收整条装得下 64K
的会话。实际读入 1.143 G 字节、监督 0.616 G 字节(训练记录里”各 0.28
GB、共 0.85 GB”是选样目标值,本文以包统计为准)。bpb
轨迹说明”中文才是新技能”:en 100 步就到 0.58 并停住,zh 从 3.02 经 400 步
1.12 到收官 0.900。但 M1 收官时模型会读不会用:探针 29/30,术语”英
$`\rightarrow`$ 中”却 0/12,英文通路
11–12/12\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94知识在,坏的是中文词形与概念之间的连接。

M2 读书阶段(16K 字节窗,6,761 步,lr 5e-6,三段续训合计 131 h):wiki 原文 :
一般语料 : 词典 = 1:1:1 按条数混合,换成监督字节就是 wiki 54% / 词典 34%
/ 对话类 6%(3.2 节),因为对话类前缀不算损失。实际读入 5.932 G、监督 4.156
G 字节。M2 之后术语”英 $`\rightarrow`$ 中”从 0/12 到 12/12(3,000
步时已达到),探针 30/30,GSM8K 对话 300 题 294;MMBench-CN 65.2%
$`\rightarrow`$ 72.2%,纯文本训练没伤到冻结的视觉塔。

两段都只混合、不先后:试点线上”窄语料先训、正常数据后补”的配方,行为被推回来了,丢掉的能力却回不来;所以
M1 从第一步就混一般对话,M2 的 wiki 也和对话一起混。

### 3.4 字节专用后训练:方法与负面经验

LD3-base 没有做任何后训练。本节记录在它之上做的一条后训练链(记作
M3)的方法与结论;这条链的权重已删除、只剩日志,不进主表。

起因是部署后的观察:LD3-base 自产回答里 46% 含 8-gram
复读(同题下另一个商用模型
6%),而且写进系统提示的写作规范它不听。提示无效就只能训进去。M3
的目标按优先级是避免复读、简洁正确的思考、按规范工作,链条四步,全部
on-policy:

1.  1.  规范 SFT:规范一般对话 10.5K 条 + 规范逻辑题答对全收约 5K 条 + 回放
        4K 条,16K 窗,lr 5e-6 WSD,259 步。
2.  2.  自采,护栏关:从训练包取”最后一轮回答之前”的前缀出题,每题采 4
        条,官方采样参数,单条上限 8,192
        字节。采样时关掉解码护栏让复读暴露,护栏掐断的样本进了训练数据就是教模型在答案段写
        \</think\>。
3.  3.  挖样与 RFT:干净 = 自己停、有 \</think\>、8-gram 重复率 $`\leq`$
        0.03、无整句重复与磕巴、规范 lint 分 $`\geq`$ 80;差 =
        顶上限、或重复率 $`\geq`$ 0.10、或整句重复 $`\geq`$
        2;逻辑题以”正确且思考最短”为 chosen。干净样本先做一轮 RFT(lr 3e-6)。
4.  4.  长度归一化 DPO:每题最多一对,chosen 取干净里 lint 最高,rejected
        取差里重复率最高。奖励 r = $`\beta`$$`\cdot`$(log p $`-`$ log
        p_ref)/len,损失 L = $`-`$log $`\sigma`$(r_c $`-`$ r_r $`-`$
        $`\gamma`$) + $`\alpha`$$`\cdot`$($`-`$log p_c/len_c),$`\beta`$ 2.0
        / $`\gamma`$ 0.5 / $`\alpha`$ 0.2,lr 5e-7。归一化是必要的:对子里
        rejected 比 chosen 长的占 99%(长度中位 634 对 4,918 字节)。

三轮结果给出三条负面经验:

- •
  跳过 RFT 直接 DPO 伤精确推理。 自采 61,600 条,差样本率 11.9%;直接
  DPO(4,460 对,140 步)把差样本率压到 7.7%,但 GSM8K 300 题贪心对话从
  97.7% 掉到 80.7%,输出均长 1,198 $`\rightarrow`$ 3,681 token。(97.7% 是
  300 题带思考贪心探针的口径,不是第 5 节主表的口径。)
- •
  RFT 先于 DPO 能拉回来。 补做”最短且对”RFT 再 DPO(7,004 对,219
  步),GSM8K 300 题回到 92.7%。
- •
  继续压复读会把思考压没。 第三轮验收差样本率只剩 0.2%,但 252
  条带思考回答里 211 条思考不到 60 个字符、中位 28 个字符,前两轮中位 136
  与 210。0.2% 大半来自”不思考”。根子在配对规则:chosen
  取”最短”会系统性选到无思考样本;后来改成 chosen 思考长度 $`\geq`$
  rejected 的
  1/4、思考语言一致、总长度最接近,让一对之间除了”病”没有别的系统差异。
  对数不够也不要训:218 对 28 步的 DPO pref_acc 0.375、复读反升。

### 3.5 深草稿 MTP

字节模型每步只出一个字节,解码步数约为原版的 4 倍,多 token
预测(MTP)草稿头是补回速度的主要手段。Qwen3.5 系原生带一个 MTP
层:fc\[5120, 10240\] 拼接下一 token 嵌入与主干隐状态,接 1 层全注意力
decoder 层,与主干共享嵌入和 lm_head(所以 384 词表直接适用),424.7M
参数;主干训完后要单独重建这一层。

草稿深度按汉字数定,不是 BPE 模型习惯的 2–3 步:一个汉字 3
字节,字内续字节近乎确定,默认 K=9(3 个汉字),之后开到 K=15(5
个汉字);训练代价 $`\propto`$ K,但 MTP 层只占主干的 1/64。LD3-base
的头冻主干只训头,K=15,1,500 步,lr 1e-4;实测后按”每轮接受 ¡ 8 字节或提速
¡ 1.5$`\times`$”触发第二轮,用模型自己写的约 1 亿字节(60,000 题)on-policy
续训,lr 5e-5,留接受长度更高的头;两轮合计约 35 GPU 时。

两条坑。其一,训练口径与服务口径差很远:试点线 K=15 的头第 1 步命中
0.935,服务里每轮只接受 5.33 字节、只快 20%,因为每位置准确率从 0.93
衰减到第 16 位的 0.40。LD3-base 的头在单卡以 K=8 运行时每轮接受 5.7
字节,16 并发 1.8$`\times`$、单流 3.3$`\times`$(5.6 节在 48G
单卡上未能复测的配置)。其二,主干一变旧头作废,必须重训;多层草稿模型与单步目标微调在我们这里都不及
1 层 MTP。

### 3.6 解码护栏

字节模型需要一层 BPE 模型不需要的解码护栏,原因在第 6
节展开。护栏实现为推理框架的自定义 logit 处理器,四个部件:

- •
  思考预算与答案预算:\<think\> 之后到预算强制写 \</think\>;\</think\>
  之后到上限强制
  \<\|im_end\|\>\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94\CJK@punctchar\CJK@uniPunct0”80”94收口后答案段照样可能循环到顶,所以两段都要预算。服务默认各
  16,384 字节。
- •
  UTF-8
  合法性掩码:前导字节之后只允许续字节(128–191),字符边界禁止裸续字节与非法前导。
- •
  循环熔断:连续 1,024 步仍在重复才强制收口 / 结束,平时不改
  logits。早期版本逐字节禁重复,试点线实测 41%
  的解码步闸门是开的(英文、LaTeX、代码里 16
  字节内重复本来就常见),思考模式赚、非思考模式亏(GPQA 思考 48.0
  $`\rightarrow`$ 60.6,非思考 60.6 $`\rightarrow`$ 53.0)。

两条使用规则。第一,必须关掉推理框架的重叠调度:重叠调度下护栏读到的输出滞后一个
token,模型刚吐出前导字节时护栏仍以为在字符边界,把合法续字节全禁掉,护栏自己制造了它要防的非法
UTF-8;三配置对照见 6.2
节。第二,护栏能救回的有上限:试点线三个护栏版本把”抽不到答案”从 77 题压到
41–53 题、收口率从 126 提到 198/198,答对数却全部是 120/198(BPE 原版
170);解码侧榨干之后剩下的是能力差距。所以护栏在”思考模式 +
有确定答案”的任务上是净收益,在要求长输出与特定结构的任务上会砍掉没写完的结构;自采训练数据时关护栏(3.4
节)。第 4
节评测里的护栏只阻止非法字节序列与超长输出,不改变合法输出的分布。

## 附录 4 实验设置

### 4.1 模型与检查点

被比较的只有两个模型:

- •
  orig:官方发布的 Qwen3.8-27B(FP8 权重,block-128 配方),字节级 BPE 词表
  248,077 项(嵌入表 248,320 行)。
- •
  LD3-base:在同一主干上把词表收缩到 384(256 个字节符号 + 128 个特殊 /
  保留 id),嵌入与输出头从各 1.27B 参数缩到约 2M(语言模型部分 26.9B
  $`\rightarrow`$ 24.4B),经两段课程(3.3 节)续训后的检查点,外加一个深度 8
  的 MTP 草稿头(3.5
  节)。本文所有表都用这一个检查点;为对齐口径,也量化成同配方的 block-128
  FP8。

LD3-base
没有做过任何面向榜单的后训练;它是”字节化是否保住了原版能力”这个问题的最直接答案。字节模型特有的后训练问题(复读、贪心跑飞)在第
6 节单独讨论方法,不进主表。

### 4.2 训练算力

8$`\times`$H200,ZeRO-3 全参续训:M1(编码阶段)47.5
h,M2(读书阶段,三段合计)131 h,主干共 178.6 h $`\approx`$ 1,430 GPU 时;MTP
头约 35 GPU 时。实际读入 7.08 G 字节、受监督 4.77 G
字节(只对助手轮算损失)。语料生成另计:自产对话 / 字典 / 词典 /
逻辑题在本机八卡上约 760 GPU 时(按生成队列日志),连同外部 API 调用折算约
2,190 GPU 时(E3_E4.md)。按 6ND 粗估主干续训约 1e21 FLOPs,与 Bolmo
同量级;数据量少一个数量级,算力不少,正文不写”便宜 N 倍”。

### 4.3 评测口径(E1 / E2)

两列在同一张 RTX 6000 Ada 48G 上、同一套服务栈(sglang
v0.5.17,FP8,单卡,无草稿,非流式,--disable-radix-cache)跑完全部榜单,避免把服务端差异算进模型差异。具体:

- •
  两档解码:思考档 temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95,把 \</think\>
  之前的内容过滤掉再判分;非思考档 temperature 0。两档都通过 chat
  template 的 enable_thinking 开关控制,模板与官方一致。
- •
  输出上限按字节 4 对齐:字节模型按字节计上限,BPE 模型取其 1/4 的 token
  数(思考档 32,768 B / 8,192 tok;非思考档 16,384 B / 4,096
  tok;LongBench-v2 5,000 B / 1,250 tok)。实测中位输出长度字节 / token
  比约 3(5.1 脚注),4 倍口径对字节模型不更紧。
- •
  逐条计数伴随每个分数:顶上限(stop_reason = max_tokens)与思考档缺
  \</think\> 的条数一并给出,避免把”没写完”和”不会”混在一起。
- •
  解码护栏:字节模型服务端带 UTF-8 合法性掩码、思考 /
  答案字节预算与熔断(3.6 节);BPE
  模型不需要也没有。护栏只阻止非法字节序列与超长输出,不改变合法输出的分布。
- •
  数据集:GSM8K
  测试全集(1,319)、MATH-500(500)、HumanEval+(164)、IFEval(541 题 / 834
  条指令)、C-Eval val(1,346)、MMLU-Pro(14 科各抽 72 题共
  1,008)、LongBench-v2(能放进上下文的 117 题)。判分用 evalscope
  的默认判分器,两列同一份代码。
- •
  bpb:留出窗口集 4 域 $`\times`$ 96 窗 $`\times`$ 4,096
  字节;字节模型直接对每字节 logprob 求和;BPE 模型对 token logprob
  求和后除以同一段文本的字节数。
- •
  单种子、单次运行。每项给逐题自助法 95% 区间与同题配对的 $`\Delta`$
  区间(2,000 次重采样,附录表 A2)。

### 4.4 字符级任务口径(E5)

- •
  题集:CUTE(leukas/cute,14 项,每项抽 400
  题)、EXECUTE(benjamin/execute)的 eng 与 zho 两语种(每项 200
  题),以及自建中文字符题 15 项(每项 200 题;繁简互转各 107
  题,受可一对一互转的自然句数量限制)。自建题的字表取自 12,126
  字的常用字表,繁简事实取 OpenCC
  STCharacters/TSCharacters(只保留一对一的字),拼音 / 笔画 / 部首取
  Unihan kMandarin/kTotalStrokes/kRSUnicode,自然句取 C-Eval 题干(8–40
  字、无 ASCII、$`\geq`$ 80% 汉字,共 675 句)。剔除 extra\_\* 后共 13,214
  题。
- •
  判分:精确匹配。先去掉”答案:”前缀、首尾引号与句号,再按题型决定是否忽略空白;只取回答的第一个非空段落。思考档只看
  \</think\> 之后。
- •
  解码:非思考档 temperature 0 为主,全部题集两列都跑;思考档只补 CUTE 全
  14 项与自建中文题各 100 题(temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95)。输出上限
  1,024 字节 / 256 token(思考档 16,384 字节 / 4,096 token)。
- •
  剔除:EXECUTE-zho 的三个 extra\_\*
  拆分(extra_c2g、extra_contains、extra_g2c,部件图式 $`\leftrightarrow`$
  整字)在公开数据里只有”Task:
  ⿰亻吏”一类输入、没有任务说明(原意为少样本),两列零样本都得
  0,不进表。EXECUTE-zho 因此与 eng 一样是 12 项。

### 4.5 效率口径(E6)

同一张卡、同一服务栈,四个配置:orig、orig + NEXTN
草稿、LD3-base、LD3-base + NEXTN 草稿(K = 8)。三个量:(1)单流解码,10
条中文与 10 条英文约 300 词的作文题,报汉字 / 秒与英文字符 / 秒而不是
token / 秒;(2)并发 16 的总吞吐,同样按字符计;(3)prefill:16,384 与 65,536
字节的中文窗口,max_tokens = 1,报首字时间(TTFT),各 3
次取中位。草稿配置要把显存占比降到 0.80、上下文降到 65,536
才能在单卡起来;起不来的配置如实记”单卡起不来”。

  单种子;逐题自助法 95% 区间(2,000 次,配对 $`\Delta`$):配对区间不含 0
  的只有 GSM8K 思考档 \[$`-`$5.3, $`-`$2.9\]、C-Eval 思考 \[$`-`$6.3,
  $`-`$2.8\] / 非思考 \[$`-`$6.5, $`-`$3.0\] 与上限主导的
  LongBench-v2;MATH-500、HumanEval+、MMLU-Pro、GSM8K 非思考的 $`\Delta`$
  区间都含 0(全表见附录表
  A2)。重采样只覆盖题目抽样方差,不覆盖解码随机性。
- •
  用时(同卡):orig 两档 7 h 44 min,LD3-base 两档 35 h 57 min($`\approx`$
  4.6$`\times`$),见 5.6。

### 5.3 中文

字节化最可能伤的是中文,所以 M1 / M2
之间用两组小探针盯着它,并在终点补一项全字复述。

- •
  术语五问。12 个中英术语(梯度下降、反向传播、哈希表、死锁等)各 5
  种问法:A 英 $`\rightarrow`$ 中只答术语、B 中 $`\rightarrow`$ 英、C
  中问中答、D 英问要求中文答、E 中问括号给英文;贪心、带思考、上限 8,192
  字节,人工判读答案段。M1 收官 A 0/12、B 6/12、C 6/12、D 11/12、E
  12/12:知识在、英文通路通,坏的是”中文词形 $`\leftrightarrow`$
  概念”的连接,这是 3.3 节”中文才是新技能”的直接证据。M2 读到 3,000 步 A
  即 12/12、B 10/12,之后不变。
- •
  30 题贪心探针。英 10 / 中 5 / 代码 5 / 格式 6 / 梯度 4,temperature
  0、上限 16,384 字节,只判 \</think\>
  之后的答案段,代码题真跑测试用例。M1 29/30 $`\rightarrow`$ M2@3000 28
  $`\rightarrow`$ M2@6000 30 $`\rightarrow`$ LD3-base
  30/30。两组探针只用于训练中决策,n 太小,不作为主结果。
- •
  12,126 字全字复述(E11)。字表与训练用字典同源(规范字 8,105 + 繁体
  4,021);每 20 字一组共 607
  组,提示”原样复述、一字不漏”,贪心、不思考,输出与输入逐字对齐,记漏字 /
  错字 / 非法字节;两列同卡同口径,各跑字典顺序与打乱重分组两遍。两遍合计
  24,252 字次,orig 错 3 字(汨 $`\rightarrow`$
  汩,以及两个生僻字抄成形近字),LD3-base 错 1 字(欽
  抄成同组前面的形近字),全部是抄成邻近或形近字,没有漏字;两列都零非法
  UTF-8、零顶上限。含 4,021
  个繁体与扩展区生僻字在内,字节模型逐字节写字没有比原版差,差别在噪声内。
